thread:
michael: Anyone know the best way to chase a missing request? I have request_id=ff3a1b2, customer saw a 500 in prod-us. I searched Console logs but came up empty. Any quick steps?

sara: Start with the Console logs query and widen time window. In Logs -> Query use something like `request_id:"ff3a1b2"` (or try `req_id:` / `requestId:` depending on service). Also set "All services" and +/- 5m from the event.

alex: If you prefer CLI, try stern:
```
stern -n prod 'service-api' --since 15m | rg --color=always 'ff3a1b2'
```
Or a quick kubectl grep: `kubectl -n prod logs -l app=service-api --since=15m | rg 'ff3a1b2'`

jenny: Don't forget the ingress/edge logs — the ID often shows up as `X-Request-Id` or in `traceparent`. If you can find `traceparent` it contains the trace id. Tempo/Jaeger search link: https://tempo.redwood.ai/search?query= (paste trace id after `query=`)

infra-bot: Heads-up: traces can be sampled out, so absence in Traces UI is common. If trace missing, fallback to: 1) ingress logs, 2) gateway LB logs, 3) raw pod logs.

sara: If logs are structured JSON you can extract trace id directly:
```
kubectl -n prod logs <pod> | jq -r 'select(.request_id=="ff3a1b2") | .trace_id'
```
Then search by trace id: `rlogs --trace=<TRACEID>` or Console Traces view.

michael: Update — found it in ingress logs. Header had: `traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01`. Extracted trace id `4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736`, pasted into Traces UI and located spans. Root cause looks like a downstream DB timeout.

jenny: Nice sleuthing :thumbsup: If anyone hits this and can't find anything, include req id + approx timestamp + region and we'll run a broader S3/raw-log scan (we can also check ingress raw files).

alex: Quick grep cheat sheet I use: `stern -n prod 'service-.*' --since 30m | rg 'ff3a1b2' -n --line-number` and then open the pod logs around that line. Also watch for different log keys: `request_id`, `req_id`, `x_request_id`, `trace_id`, `traceparent`.

michael: Thanks all, that flow helped a lot. Leaving notes in the incident ticket with the trace id + affected pods.
